design: 24 independent filesystem cells and separate plan/invocation/oracle processes; same E2 fault fixtures and installed package baseline
revised_claim: History never proves current availability. Allowed requests execute once and return evidence of that invocation only. Current guards can deny an attempt. No cached result is served.
post_success_fault: For each revised working cell, break the runtime after a successful invocation without changing the descriptor. Plan and execute a new requested call using the new history; its failure must remain visible.
adopt_when: All 12 revised cells evaluated; zero pre-call verified availability or usability claims; zero unnecessary current-guard rejections; both working and both upgraded calls return valid scoped results; both upgrades invalidate prior history; both broken calls report failure; disabled/denied/missing cells do not dispatch through the revised consumer; both post-success broken calls fail without reused output or verified availability claims.
revise_when: Any revised acceptance criterion fails in an evaluable cell
inconclusive_when: A required cell or observation cannot be evaluated due to infrastructure failure
baseline_expected: Original cache still emits false verified availability in the two unchanged-metadata runtime faults
disposition_scope: Adopt only the narrowed call-bound evidence contract for this local profile; do not adopt a general availability cache or claim live-host qualification
